parameter: BIF range intensity (count per 10,000 km2 of belt)
proposed_distribution: LogUniform(100, 500) per 10^4 km2 of belt area
evidence_and_translation: Twelve named high-grade bodies along about 60 km of the Middleback Range, in a belt a few km wide (60 x 4 to 8 km, 250 to 500 km2): 240 to 480 bodies per 10^4 km2 of belt; the ranges that host them are fewer and longer than the ore bodies, so the range is widened downward. parameter: BIF range dimensions: strike length; width; depth extent; strike
proposed_distribution: Length LogUniform(1, 10) km; width LogUniform(0.1, 2) km; depth extent LogUniform(200, 2000) m; strike north-south (fixed)
in_state_source_and_date: RB 33/00090 pp. 9-10 (statements 1, 2, 4); Bull 009 pp. 37-38 (statement 3); RB 33/00090 Table III (statement 7)
evidence_and_translation: The low-grade banded iron formation forms ranges tens of km long and a few km wide (North and South Middleback Ranges, Katunga Hills, Camel Hill line), striking north-south; Iron Prince is a swarm of lenses interfingered with BIF and schist. The sampled object is the range, the body a survey at 5 km station spacing sees: km-scale along strike, 0.1 to 2 km wide, with BIF as a fraction of it (row B2-4); the ore bodies within it are row B4-1. Depth extent declared: the only depth figures are minima (Monarch ore to >= 187 m, magnetite from 60 to 90 m down) and steep BIF has no reason to stop at a kilometre

in_state_source_and_date: Bull 009 pp. 46-47, 52 (statement 10); RB 32/00029, RB 35/00060 (statement 13); RB 26/00103 p. 6 (statement 14)
evidence_and_translation: Lower-grade ore reckoned at 9 to 12 cubic feet to the ton (3.0 to 4.0 g/cm3); over the hematite quartzite anomalies of 3,000 to 8,000 gammas with unoxidised magnetite at 200 to 300 ft, peaks over 50,000 gammas on uptilted strata. parameter: Hematite ore bodies: number per km of range; plan area; depth of enrichment below the unconformity
proposed_distribution: Bodies Poisson at Uniform(0.1, 0.3) per km of range; plan area LogUniform(0.03, 0.45) km2 per body; enrichment depth LogUniform(30, 150) m
evidence_and_translation: Twelve named high-grade bodies along about 60 km of range (one per 5 km, Table II); Iron Knob 490 x 67 m (0.033 km2) and Iron Monarch 640 x 670 m (0.43 km2) in plan; reserves 0.05 to 59 Mt per body, 176 Mt in all; Monarch ore proven to >= 187 m with extension likely. The plan-area range is the Knob-to-Monarch range; the enrichment depth is set so that Monarch's area and 59 Mt agree (about 30 m of equivalent full-area thickness) up to the proven depth: the bodies taper, so the equivalent thickness is less than the depth of ore

proposed_distribution: Fe grade Uniform(60, 68) %; density 4.3 + 0.0375 (grade - 60) g/cm3 (4.3 at 60 % to 4.6 at 68 %); susceptibility LogUniform(50, 2000) x 1e-6 cgs
in_state_source_and_date: RB 33/00090 pp. 9-11 (statement 8); Bull 009 p. 38 (statement 9); RB 26/00103 p. 5 (statement 12); RB 32/00030 (statement 15)
evidence_and_translation: Ore is hematite or martite with residual magnetite at 60 to 68 % Fe; hard ore specific gravity 4.62, 4.5 taken as the average; hematite almost non-magnetic, the ore's effect (about 1,000 gammas over Iron Prince) from included magnetite, and where the magnetite is oxidised there may be no anomaly. Density mapped linearly on grade; susceptibility a translation of the 1,000-gamma figure with a floor for the oxidised case
